answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can let each key's bond rise with the size of the reef it belongs to. Every epoch, keys whose answers, timing or network inlet overlap are linked into one reef, and each member must keep 40×k POA locked, where k is the reef size: a lone agent holds 40, while a 1,000-key reef locks 40,000 per key, 40 million in all, against roughly 0.5 million of epoch pay. A key that fails to top up is frozen and its bond slashed. For unlinked agents the cost curve is a mesa, flat at 40. Weakness: paraphrased clones evade linking, so jurors still score reuse.
